title: The Dark Truth About Haré+Guu
description:
Evolution does not optimize for happiness — Haré+Guu shows exactly where that breaks. Haré+Guu (Japanese: ジャングルはいつもハレのちグゥ, Hepburn: Janguru wa Itsumo Hare nochi Gū; lit. 'The Jungle Was Always Sunny, Then Came Guu') is a Japanese manga series written and illustrated by Renjuro Kindaichi which ran in Square Enix's Monthly Shōnen Gangan magazine from 1997 to 2002. The series focuses on the story of a ten-year-old boy named Haré who lives in the jungle and his misadventures with Guu, a liminal being who usually presents herself as a young girl.

After some heartfelt goodbyes with their classmates, the kids of the jungle return home except for Wigle who stays to attend college. The series focuses on the story of a ten-year-old boy named Haré who lives in the jungle and his misadventures with Guu, a liminal being who usually presents herself as a young girl.

What looks like free choice in Haré+Guu is older than choice itself. It was adapted into a 26-episode anime television series, followed by two OVA sequels: Haré+Guu DELUXE and Haré+Guu FINAL. It then flashes forward to the present where Haré is a typical boy living in an unnamed village in an unidentified jungle with his lazy mother Weda.

Nobody designed the part of Haré+Guu you experience — it was inherited. On his way back from his errand of fetching bananas, a large dark being overtakes him. Scared, he runs back to the house where his mom has decided to have a new guest, a cute girl named Guu.

Every serious account of Haré+Guu eventually collides with the question of who is deciding. The next morning, Haré wakes up to find Guu a completely different person who is no longer cute, social, or energetic. Guu mostly remains quiet and ignorant of things while Haré has to show her around and explain things.

Nihilism is not the conclusion of Haré+Guu — it is the floor you stand on while examining it. She swallows Haré but, instead of dying, he is taken to another world in Guu's stomach. There he meets Seiichi and Tomoyo, a couple who has accepted their fate in Guu's stomach.

The selfish-gene reading of Haré+Guu makes it less romantic and far more precise. After Guu spits Haré out, she accompanies him to school where she meets all of Haré's schoolmates (whom she swallows and spits back out) and the village elder (whose chest hair she rips out). Clive who came from the city and turns out to be Haré's long-lost dad.

Freud is not dead; he is simply no longer allowed to be the whole answer. Most of the other characters start developing personalities and eccentricities of their own. Guu goes from being silent to being extremely cynical and sarcastic towards Haré and the others.

The feeling that Haré+Guu means something is a chemical event with an evolutionary address. Guu starts causing shenanigans around the jungle that are meant to keep her amused (like holding a contest for Weda). She adds another resident to her stomach world, Miss Hiroko Yamada, and shows an adult form that she uses to defend Haré.

Nothing in Haré+Guu was built for you — it was built for reproduction. Another person who appears is Dama, a hairdresser from the next village over who obsesses over her long-lost husband with white hair that she mistakes Dr. Bel and Asio, two servants who worked for Weda in her past life, visit the jungle.

The psychology underneath Haré+Guu is simpler and older than the story on top. They relieve Haré of his chores around the house and Haré enjoys having to do less work. Guu causes more disasters around the jungle such as creating a blizzard and bringing down the wrath of Dama upon Clive.

Behind Haré+Guu sits an animal brain negotiating with a story it tells itself. Clive finally dyes his hair black to have Dama leave him alone. Haré finds out from Asio the circumstances behind Weda leaving her past life and why Weda is living in they jungle.

The nihilist does not deny Haré+Guu — he only refuses to flatter it. Weda eventually forces Bel and Asio to tell the actual reason they came to the jungle: to bring Weda and Haré back to the city since her father had recently died. Haré, Weda, Guu, Bel, and Asio make it to the city where they are met by Robert, a personal bodyguard hired to protect Haré and Weda.

What culture calls destiny in Haré+Guu is usually just selection pressure wearing a suit. When Haré and Guu are held hostage by a bank robber, Weda and Robert team up to proficiently take out the robber, safely returning Haré and Guu. Haré easily adjusts to luxurious life in the mansion while Weda is bored.

The genes do not care about Haré+Guu; they care about copies. Clive comes to the city where he finally is able to convey his feelings for Weda, ensuring them to be a couple whenever Weda returns. Guu causes more hijinks by swallowing up all the servants in a game of tag.

Take away the meaning and Haré+Guu still functions — that is the disturbing part. While Haré is running away, he runs into his long-lost grandmother Sharon. Try as he might, all seemed lost as Weda was bored enough to want to return to the jungle much to Bel and Asio's chagrin.

The unconscious does not argue with Haré+Guu; it simply acts first. Just as Weda was about to visit her mom, Sharon rides up and the two make up. Haré, Weda, and Guu are back in the jungle with Clive now living permanently with Haré.

Haré+Guu feels chosen. The evidence says it was installed. Haré meets the new teacher while Lazy-Sensei was sick named Miss Yumi. She ends up falling for Haré and harassing him for the next two arcs despite their age difference.

The bleak reading of Haré+Guu is also the most testable one. Meanwhile, the village elder's chest hair gets so out of control he is swallowed by it enough for him to disappears for the rest of the arc. Weda announces she's pregnant and Clive decides that it is time to marry.

Modern psychology keeps rediscovering what the pessimists said first about Haré+Guu. After they marry, Haré starts hating the idea of another sibling as he will be the one to take care of the child due to his parents' laziness. Guu takes him back to the past where he inadvertently ran into Weda.

The self that experiences Haré+Guu is a committee, not a king. It turns out she is lazy due to the advice he gave her to be more honest with herself. He makes up a fake name while meeting Weda which Weda uses in the present to call her second child.

Reproduction explains more of Haré+Guu than any philosophy dares to admit. The bank robber returns to exact his revenge on Weda for foiling him. When it looked like he was about to win, Dama shows up at the last minute to fight the bank robber.
Once you see Haré+Guu as an adaptation, the mystery mostly evaporates. Bel misses Weda and sends out a video letter to the jungle. Weda agrees to come back to the city to visit Bel and her mom.

The story Haré+Guu tells about itself is the last thing to be trusted. Haré becomes bored, so Weda enrolls him in school where he meets and instantly falls in love with Rita. Unfortunately, it works against Haré because the school bullies get jealous of the new friendship he has formed with Rita; they bully him.

Meaning is not found in Haré+Guu — it is manufactured for it. Haré finds out that he is nothing special to Rita because she likes to feel superior by being nice to everyone and not making any enemies. Eventually, Rita sees Haré for the friend he is and learns to care about others.

The cold light on Haré+Guu leaves the facts intact and only the comfort removed. Weda resolves things at home, which allows Haré and Guu to return to the jungle. The village elder, who is basically a hairball now, is found while Haré gets help with Ame thanks to Adult Guu and the three residents in Guu's stomach.

Haré+Guu did not evolve to be understood — only to be survived. Dama returns as one of the assassins hired to kill Weda, but Robert manages to talk her into going back to life with her husband. After seven attempts on her life, Weda resolves to go to the city to bring the fight to her siblings.

The honest version of Haré+Guu starts by giving up the comforting part. Weda goes to the city to settle things, and she brings all the kids from the jungle with her. They first run into trouble when two more assassins, Alex and Shirly, cause their plane to crash on an island.

Strip Haré+Guu of its poetry and the mechanism underneath is stranger. On the island, they meet a muscle man named QP who becomes a rival to Robert and a bodyguard for Weda. When they get off the island they return to Weda's family's mansion where everyone makes plans to go to school.

Nobody designed the part of Haré+Guu you experience — it was inherited. She also ate Dama's sister Tama who tells them the whole story behind her and her sister. Weda makes up with her siblings but Haré and his cousin, Alva, still fight.

Every serious account of Haré+Guu eventually collides with the question of who is deciding. Guu is kidnapped by Haré and Guu — from a half year in the future — who came to find Dama and her sister. Haré, Guu, and their future counterparts find the two, but it is too late.
